explanation: C uses semicolons to end expression statements, return statements, and ordinary declarations. A line break is usually whitespace, so splitting two statements across lines does not separate them by itself.
exampleExplanation: The declaration, the update, and the return each end with their own semicolon. These are independent statements.
misconceptions: The diagnostic can point at the next token because that is where the compiler discovered the missing boundary.
A closing brace does not always need a semicolon. A function body ends with a brace, while a structure definition used as a declaration ends with a semicolon.

reference.title: Local C reference on statement boundaries
reference.text: An expression statement has an optional expression followed by a semicolon. A return statement has the keyword return, an optional expression, and a semicolon. A compound statement is a sequence of declarations and statements enclosed by braces. The three clauses of a for header have their own punctuation rules.
